newsitem.title: USA: NABL urges bond attys to eye conflicts of interest.
newsitem.headline: NABL urges bond attys to eye conflicts of interest.

text.p: The National Association of Bond Lawyers urged its members on Monday to consider disclosing in official statements possible conflicts of interest in the bond deals they are handling.

"Consideration should be given to disclosure in the Official Statement of contingent fee arrangements with certain experts, including legal counsel," NABL says in its first update of its "Model Bond Opinion Report" since 1987.

"Likewise, bond counsel should consider disclosure in the Official Statement of other interests of bond counsel in the transaction or its conflicts in representation," says the 37-page report prepared by NABL's Committee on Opinions.
The panel is chaired by bond attorney Michael Buden, of Wolf, Block, Schorr and Solis-Cohen in Philadelphia. NABL plans to debate the report at its upcoming Washington Seminar May 8-9.
The guidelines come amid increased attention by federal enforcement officials on conflicts of interest involving bond dealers, lawyers, and issuers in muni bond deals.
